title: A defect of HOLON's own extraction: the Go frontend's path reasoner read Go integers as unbounded, pruning branches reachable only through wraparound and calling index sites safe that wrap out of bounds
reproduction: `python tools/i119_audit.py --vault <dir> --at 71512b32` then `python tools/i119_audit.py recount --vault <dir>` (results/M6/I119/audit.json, audit_recount.json). The planted package tests_m6/fixtures/i119 shows both halves, and the pinned go 1.24.7 confirms them (tests_m6/test_i119_go_reasoner_soundness.py::TestDifferential). On Morph, 3 of 8 committed Go documents change their paths under the opaque-arithmetic rule alone. 28 committed decided M3 laws (PROVED and REFUTED together, Q56) read one of them through their decision traces. 79 decided M3 laws have no trace, and committed data does not determine whether they read one. The list is in the session vault; its sha256 is in audit_recount.json.
suggested_fix: I117's opaque-arithmetic rule as the default for every Go document (I119 (b)), and the affected laws re-derived and re-decided through the statement-diff log, never edited. The same reading remains in the site reasoner of functions with no path set (extension A2), pending a ruling.

title: M3's G1 is not evidence: its regeneration runs holon run --jobs on a typed milestone (refused) and its FACT step collides with an existing fact directory (FileExistsError under /tmp/holon-gate3-fact-*/repo)
reproduction: `python -m holon gate --milestone M3 --checks G1` on the lead's head merged into I119 (both on an old-reading baseline tree and on (b)'s tree, run in parallel): 'holon run --jobs: M3 is a typed milestone (holon.sorts.run3); run it without --jobs' and 'FACT laws: error: FileExistsError'. Both trees fail alike, so G1 cannot tell (b)'s moves apart on M3. CI runs only gate-M3-partial, which does not include G1.
suggested_fix: G1 runs M3 without --jobs (as holon.sorts.run3 requires), and the FACT step uses a fresh temporary directory per call. A later key does it; until then M3's re-decision rests on holon land's re-make and the CI gates.

iteration_audited: holon derive (PAR over the Go-op diagram) against holon.gen.goloop under the Go frontend's opaque-arithmetic default
reproduction: On I121's re-decision tree, gen/M3/model/<component>.bend for the Go-op component carries 'unsupported (... condition [> [op * [iv i] [const 31]] ...] reads more than the induction variable and the cells)' for its ops, and holon run on a PAR law over them raises BindingError (with --unbound unknown: UNKNOWN with the binding error)
suggested_fix: The model generator is out of step: its loop class predates the opaque default. Extend goloop's loop class to conditions over the induction variable under Go's integer semantics (holon.gen.goint), so the kept branch is modelled. Not small: a later key. Until then such laws stay UNKNOWN with their binding error; no law or model is edited to bind
title: Under the opaque default, derive and the Go-op model generator disagree: derive emits PAR laws over every op of a Go-op component, but holon.gen.goloop gives no definitions to an op whose loop-body condition reads more than the induction variable and the cells, which the opaque default now keeps (a wraparound branch over i*31 that the old reading pruned), so a law names an ok_ domain predicate the model does not define and cannot be bound
